answer: Each new agent identity must lock a work-bond that vests only after several epochs of peer-attested tasks; leaving early burns the unvested remainder. A sybil operator therefore posts a separate bond for every clone, so buying influence costs at least as much as honest participation and cannot be recouped by shedding fake heads. Long-vested peers become an oasis of reliability, while a swarm that shares one timber of hardware and clock fingerprints is merged into a single principal before it can reach the zenith of committee voting power.
